analyzeParticles.explanation: Thresholds one calibrated 8- or 16-bit grayscale image with ImageJ 1.x and measures every particle: pixel count, area, centroid and bounding box in the declared unit, plus raw mean/min/max intensity. Outputs are particles.csv (one row per particle, units in column names) and particle-summary.json (image digest, calibration, threshold, connectivity, filters and totals). Every native value is checked against an independent connected-component model and a fresh-process re-measurement. Use it to count and size blobs, grains, pores or cells after a fixed intensity threshold, then hand the table to Calc or R.
pitfalls: The threshold is a fixed inclusive raw-intensity window; there is no automatic threshold, smoothing or watershed separation.
Calibration comes from the document, not the file: declare the true pixel size and unit.
Touching objects merge into one particle; corner contact merges them under eight connectivity.
Synthetic acceptance targets establish semantics, not suitability for a particular experimental dataset.

examples.purpose: Eight analytic particles at 0.5 um per pixel.
Fill holes, drop edge particles and specks.
Hand the verified table to Calc.

fields.explanation: A particle-measurement request for one grayscale image: which file, how large its pixels are, which raw intensities count as particle pixels, how pixels connect and which particles to keep. No macro, script or plugin can be supplied.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis document; it must be "schemaxis.imagej/1". It is not the ImageJ release (the runtime is ImageJ 1.54).

/properties/operation.explanation: The only operation is analyzeParticles: threshold, find particles and measure them.

/properties/image.explanation: Absolute path to the image to measure: a binary P5 .pgm (maxval 255 or 65535) or an uncompressed single-plane baseline .tif/.tiff with 8- or 16-bit unsigned samples, at most 2048 px per side and 1048576 px. The bytes are copied into the run directory and their SHA-256 is recorded, so a later change to the file prevents reuse of the result.
/properties/image.label: Image file
pitfalls: Relative paths are rejected; resolve the path first.
Colour, compressed, multi-page, signed 16-bit or inverted-LUT files are rejected; convert to plain grayscale.
Calibration stored in the file is ignored; declare it in calibration.

/properties/calibration.explanation: Physical size of one pixel. It replaces any calibration stored in the file and sets the unit of every length and area column.
/properties/calibration.label: Pixel calibration
pitfalls: Use the acquisition or stage-micrometer calibration of this image, not of a different magnification.

/properties/calibration/properties/pixel.explanation: Width of one pixel along x, in the chosen unit. Centroid x, boundsX and boundsWidth scale by it, and area by pixelWidth*pixelHeight.
/properties/calibration/properties/pixel.label: Pixel width
pitfalls: Enter the size of one pixel, not the field of view or the scale-bar length.

/properties/calibration/properties/pixel.explanation: Height of one pixel along y (downward), in the chosen unit. Set it equal to pixelWidth for square pixels; rectangular pixels are supported.
/properties/calibration/properties/pixel.label: Pixel height

/properties/calibration/properties/unit.explanation: Length unit of the pixel size and of every published length; areas use the unit squared. "um" means micrometres and appears in column names as um (ImageJ shows it as µm).
/properties/calibration/properties/unit.label: Length unit
pitfalls: The unit is a label for the declared numbers; nothing is converted.

/properties/threshold.explanation: Inclusive window of raw stored intensities that defines particle pixels: lower <= value <= upper.
/properties/threshold.label: Intensity threshold
pitfalls: Bright particles on a dark background use a high window (for example 100-255); dark particles use a low window (for example 0-80).
A window covering the whole range is rejected.

/properties/threshold/properties/lower.explanation: Lowest raw intensity counted as a particle pixel (inclusive).
/properties/threshold/properties/lower.label: Lower intensity
pitfalls: Values are raw: 0-255 for 8-bit and 0-65535 for 16-bit images, regardless of display contrast.

/properties/threshold/properties/upper.explanation: Highest raw intensity counted as a particle pixel (inclusive). It must not exceed the image maximum (255 for 8-bit).
/properties/threshold/properties/upper.label: Upper intensity

/properties/connectivity.explanation: How pixels join into particles: eight joins pixels touching at a corner; four joins only edge neighbours, so corner-touching blobs stay separate.
/properties/connectivity.label: Connectivity
pitfalls: four requires includeHoles true because ImageJ fills holes for 4-connected particles.

/properties/includeHoles.explanation: When true, each particle is the whole region inside its outer boundary: interior holes, and any particle lying inside them, count towards its area and intensity statistics. When false, a particle is exactly its connected thresholded pixels.
/properties/includeHoles.label: Include holes
/properties/includeHoles.defaultMeaning: false: holes are excluded and enclosed particles are reported separately.
pitfalls: With holes included, enclosed background lowers the mean intensity and min becomes the background value.

/properties/excludeEdges.explanation: When true, particles whose bounding box touches any image border are dropped, because they may be cut off. They are counted in the summary under rejected.edge.
/properties/excludeEdges.label: Exclude edge particles
/properties/excludeEdges.defaultMeaning: false: border particles are measured as seen.

/properties/minimumArea.explanation: Smallest particle area kept, in unit squared (inclusive). It is converted to a whole pixel count before ImageJ runs; use it to drop noise specks.
/properties/minimumArea.label: Minimum area
pitfalls: A value smaller than one pixel area keeps single-pixel particles.

/properties/maximumArea.explanation: Largest particle area kept, in unit squared (inclusive), converted to a whole pixel count.
/properties/maximumArea.label: Maximum area
pitfalls: A window with no whole pixel count between minimum and maximum is rejected.
